transcript.text: Thank you all for joining me today. As you know, the district is considering a classroom pilot of an adaptive writing platform for the coming fall term. The vendor has offered a no-cost pilot, and the platform can provide individualized writing prompts and feedback to students. Before I approve this proposal, I need to hear from each of you on the operational aspects that fall within your areas of expertise. The draft proposal currently doesn't specify several key details — the participating grade, data settings, teacher support, privacy review, or family orientation arrangements. I'd like to go around and get your findings on these gaps. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I'd like to share what I found when I observed this platform in action. I observed the platform in two seventh-grade classrooms, and what I saw is that the useful feedback from the system depended on a six-week cycle — and critically, that cycle required one coached teacher-planning session each week. Without that regular coaching support, the feedback didn't translate into meaningful instructional gains. I recorded this in my coaching notes, but I should note those notes haven't been attached to the draft proposal, so this finding hasn't been part of the formal review until now.
